source_evidence: With a traditional 401(k), the tax benefit is upfront. With a Roth 401(k), the tax benefit comes later.
answer: A 401(k) plan may offer traditional and Roth account options, which differ in when taxes apply. With a traditional 401(k), contributions and investment earnings are tax-deferred, and taxes are paid when the money is withdrawn. With a Roth 401(k), contributions are made with after-tax dollars; earnings and withdrawals are generally tax-free. The source says you can allocate money between the two options, including contributing to both.
